standard_prerequisites.name: The groups G(R) and H(R) and the monogenic presentation of a point of H
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the description of a point of H(R) by an A-algebra map A[t, 1/(pi^ell t + 1)] -> R and of a point of G(R) by A[s, 1/(pi s + 1)] -> R
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the objects between which the map is shown to be surjective.

standard_prerequisites.name: The monogenic extension statement for the polynomial Phi
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma stating that setting s to a root b of Phi(s) - a gives a compatible A-algebra map
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the unique compatible map producing the lift.

core_obligations: Translate the point (proof lines 14689-14692): let h in H(R) correspond to the A-algebra map A[t, 1/(pi^ell t + 1)] -> R sending t to a in A.
Find the root (proof lines 14693-14695): since Phi(s) is monic there is b in A with Phi(b) = a.

Lift (proof lines 14696-14698): by the monogenic lemma, sending s to b gives a unique A-algebra map A[s, 1/(pi s + 1)] -> R compatible with the given one, which corresponds to an element g in G(R) mapping to h.
proof_roadmap: Read the point h as a map on the t-chart.
Apply the monogenic lemma to produce the compatible map on the s-chart, giving the lift.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states the surjectivity of G(R) -> H(R) for an absolutely integrally closed A-algebra (statement lines 14682-14686). The proof (proof lines 14688-14698) reads a point of H as a map on the t-chart, uses monicity of Phi to solve Phi(b) = a, and applies the monogenic lemma to build the compatible map on the s-chart. H2: one explicit lifting, written out.
